messages:
ben_support: Hey team — customer X is hitting repeated 429s when they prefetch large contexts (around 60–70k tokens) and fan out ~12 parallel requests. They also saw a couple of 401s during the same window. Asking for per-model RPM/TPM and max concurrency for the rwd-64k and rwd-32k variants and quick mitigation advice.

cory_infra: Thanks. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and the request sizes? Also which API key / org? 429s + 401s together usually point to quota exhaustion + a temporary auth rotation glitch.

ben_support: Repro snippet from customer (sanitized):

curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer SK-XXXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-64k","input":"<~65k tokens payload>","max_tokens":512}'

They say 12 concurrent workers each doing prefetch, bursts aligned to every 30s.

cory_infra: That pattern explains it — sustained bursts + large context increases token throughput (TPM) quickly. Quick facts (internal guidance): rwd-64k typically has lower RPM/TPM and lower concurrency than rwd-32k due to memory/KV pressure. If you need to prod the exact quota, we can check the customer's account but mitigation first: reduce parallelism to <=6, stagger prefetch, and add exponential backoff with jitter.

ben_support: Customer asked exact numbers to justify a Dedicated quote. Can we provide typical default caps?

dana_eng: For reference (typical defaults, subject to account tiers):
- rwd-64k: ~50 RPM, ~30 TPM, max concurrency ~4–8 depending on region
- rwd-32k: ~120 RPM, ~80 TPM, max concurrency ~12–16
These are ballpark — enterprise/Dedicated can be raised.

ben_support: Noted. Customer also saw transient 401s — could that be related?

cory_infra: 401s during heavy bursts usually mean their API key hit a backend auth race (token refresh, or simultaneous rotational calls). Ask customer to confirm no key rotation occurred and to check logs for 401s with error "invalid_api_key" vs "rate_limited". If it's rotation, short-lived 401s will stop once rotation completes.

alice_cs: I'll propose two immediate options to the customer: 1) short-term: stagger requests to 3–5 concurrent, add 200ms base backoff + jitter, reduce prefetch window; 2) long-term: apply for Dedicated or raise per-model quotas (we can start approval). Which do they prefer?

ben_support: They want a mitigation now and a capacity quote. I'll send these steps and request account id for quota check.

redwood-bot: Deploy successful: autoscaler patch reverted prefetch burst smoothing (deployed 02:16 UTC) — FYI might change observed behavior for some customers.

cory_infra: One more suggestion — enable prefix/KV cache for repeated context to avoid reprocessing large prefix on each request. If they cannot, advise converting prefetch into asynchronous background fetches and caching outputs.

ben_support: Action items: 1) get account id + logs for 401/429, 2) recommend immediate fanout reduction + backoff + caching, 3) engage sales for Dedicated quote. I'll update thread after customer reply. (reaction :thumbsup:)
